# Slug-document interfaces

The three kinds are the same product: per-user slug + label + LaTeX body + cached PDF. Master resumes and project masters already duplicate this through [relocation_jobs/mcp/repo.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/repo.py), [relocation_jobs/mcp/service.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/service.py), [relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py](relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py), and [relocation_jobs/static/js/apply.js](relocation_jobs/static/js/apply.js). Interview notes already have UI + tests (`/api/mcp/interview-notes`, `save_interview_note`, `interview_note_pdf_filename`) but **no backend** — the migration is registered in [relocation_jobs/core/migrations.py](relocation_jobs/core/migrations.py) (`mcp_interview_notes_v1`) without `_migrate_mcp_interview_notes_v1`, and repo/service/routes/names are empty.

Variance that belongs in the kind, not in another copy of the UPSERT:

- table name (`mcp_master_resumes` / `mcp_project_masters` / `mcp_interview_notes`)
- slug error label (`"master resume slug"` vs `"project master slug"`)
- PDF filename helper
- `tex_for_render`: masters compile as a full document; projects and notes wrap a fragment via the existing `wrap_project_fragment_for_pdf` (interview-note render tests require `\documentclass` around `\subsection*`)

Applications / cover letters stay out of this. They are keyed by `idempotency_key`, not slug.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  routes["HTTP / MCP named tools"] --> wrappers["list_master_resumes / save_project_master / ..."]
  wrappers --> engine["generic list/get/save/render"]
  engine --> repo["generic SQL in repo.py"]
  kinds["MASTER / PROJECT / NOTE"] -.->|"implements SlugDocumentKind"| engine
```

## Contract (the interface)

Add [relocation_jobs/mcp/ports.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/ports.py) (same pattern as [relocation_jobs/fetch/ports.py](relocation_jobs/fetch/ports.py)):

```python
class SlugDocumentKind(Protocol):
    table: str
    slug_kind: str
    missing_label: str
    def pdf_filename(self, full_name: str, slug: str) -> str: ...
    def tex_for_render(self, content: str) -> str: ...
```

Three frozen dataclass records implement it (`MASTER_RESUME`, `PROJECT_MASTER`, `INTERVIEW_NOTE`). That is the whole public contract a new kind has to fill in.

Unify [relocation_jobs/mcp/types.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/types.py) `MasterResumeSummary` + `ProjectMasterSummary` into one `SlugDocumentSummary` (identical fields today). Keep the old names as aliases if MCP/tests still import them.

## Shared engine (identical behavior once)

SQL stays in `repo.py` (layer rule). One private implementation parameterized by `kind.table` for list / get_row / read_content / save (upsert + null PDF when content changes) / read_pdf / save_pdf. Named wrappers stay (`save_master_resume`, `save_project_master`, `save_interview_note`, …) so MCP tools and existing tests do not churn.

Service: one `list_documents` / `get_document_detail` / `save_document` / `render_document_pdf` / `read_document_pdf_download` taking a kind. Named wrappers delegate. Render loop is the current `render_master_pdf` body with `kind.tex_for_render` and `kind.pdf_filename`.

HTTP: one `register_slug_document_routes(app, prefix, kind)` in [relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py](relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py) covering `GET/PUT {prefix}`, `GET/PUT {prefix}/<slug>`, `GET {prefix}/<slug>/pdf`, `POST {prefix}/<slug>/render`. Call it three times for `/api/mcp/master-resumes`, `/project-masters`, `/interview-notes`.

JS: replace the tripled editor in [relocation_jobs/static/js/apply.js](relocation_jobs/static/js/apply.js) with `createSlugDocumentEditor({ apiBase, ids, copy })`. Three configs. Split to `apply-documents.js` only if `apply.js` stays unreadable after the factory lands.

## Interview notes as the third kind

This is the first consumer, not a fourth copy.

- Implement `_migrate_mcp_interview_notes_v1` (same columns as project masters, including `pdf_bytes` / `pdf_updated_at`)
- Add `interview_note_pdf_filename` in [relocation_jobs/mcp/names.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/names.py) (tests already specify `jane_doe_interview_star.pdf` / `interview_star.pdf`)
- MCP tools in [relocation_jobs/mcp/server.py](relocation_jobs/mcp/server.py): `list_interview_notes`, `get_interview_note`, `save_interview_note`; include count/slugs in `get_mcp_status`

Existing tests in [tests/mcp/test_mcp_service.py](tests/mcp/test_mcp_service.py), [tests/web/test_mcp_panel.py](tests/web/test_mcp_panel.py), and [tests/mcp/test_names.py](tests/mcp/test_names.py) become the acceptance bar. Add a small contract test that all three kinds satisfy list → save → detail → pdf-invalidate-on-content-change.

## What we are not doing

- No ABC class hierarchy and no table-name string API without a typed kind
- No collapsing these into one DB table (existing tables stay)
- No pulling tailored applications into the Protocol
- No extra facade modules (`documents.py` / `store.py`); ports + kinds + generic functions in the files that already own the work

## Interview notes (after you are invited)

Master resumes and project masters exist to **create a tailored CV** for a posting. Interview notes are a **different document, at a later step**.

The CV is already tailored and submitted. The user has been **invited to interview** (e.g. Adyen). They write notes to **pass that interview** — not to rewrite the résumé.

| Document | When | What it is for |
|----------|------|----------------|
| Master resume | Always | Archive; source for a tailored CV |
| Project master | Always | Evidence bank for mirror bullets on the tailored CV |
| Tailored CV | Per application | The PDF they submit |
| Interview notes | After an invite | Prep for **that** conversation; downloadable; a glossary over time |

### Purpose

- Prepare for a specific upcoming interview: likely questions, stories mapped to the resume they submitted, project depth, what this company / interviewer will probe, questions to ask them.
- Ground notes in the **tailored or master CV**, relevant **project masters**, the **job description**, and company research.
- Store and download from `/apply` → Notes so each invite has a durable PDF.
- Over many interviews, the set of notes becomes a **glossary**. Prior company notes help prepare for similar roles later.
- Secondary only: a note might later inform a master or a new tailored CV. That is not why the document exists.

### When to use the tools

| Tool | When |
|------|------|
| `list_interview_notes` | Starting prep for an invite, or mining the glossary |
| `get_interview_note` | Reading one company's notes, or an older similar interview |
| `save_interview_note` | Writing/updating notes for this invite — slug like `adyen` |

Do **not** call these during reframe phases 0–5. Do **not** save skim-budget drops as notes. Do **not** paste notes into `save_tailored_tex`.

1. Confirm company + role. Load `get_job_context` (JD), the tailored/master CV used for that application, and a JD-aligned `get_project_master` if stories need project depth.
2. `list_interview_notes` — reuse useful material from earlier interviews.
3. Draft notes: company thesis, what they will test, stories mapped to the resume, questions to ask, research to do, honest gaps.
4. `save_interview_note(slug, content, label=...)` — kebab-case company slug, human label (e.g. `Adyen interview`).
5. User renders and downloads the PDF on the panel.

## Interview notes (after you are invited)

Master resumes and project masters exist to **create a tailored CV** for a posting. Interview notes are a **different document, at a later step**.

The CV is already tailored and submitted. The user has been **invited to interview** (e.g. Adyen). They write notes to **pass that interview** — not to rewrite the résumé.

| Document | When | What it is for |
|----------|------|----------------|
| Master resume | Always | Archive; source for a tailored CV |
| Project master | Always | Evidence bank for mirror bullets on the tailored CV |
| Tailored CV | Per application | The PDF they submit |
| Interview notes | After an invite | Prep for **that** conversation; downloadable; a glossary over time |

### Purpose

- Prepare for a specific upcoming interview: likely questions, stories mapped to the resume they submitted, project depth, what this company / interviewer will probe, questions to ask them.
- Ground notes in the **tailored or master CV**, relevant **project masters**, the **job description**, and company research.
- Store and download from `/apply` → Notes so each invite has a durable PDF.
- Over many interviews, the set of notes becomes a **glossary**. Prior company notes help prepare for similar roles later.
- Secondary only: a note might later inform a master or a new tailored CV. That is not why the document exists.

### When to use the tools

| Tool | When |
|------|------|
| `list_interview_notes` | Starting prep for an invite, or mining the glossary |
| `get_interview_note` | Reading one company's notes, or an older similar interview |
| `save_interview_note` | Writing/updating notes for this invite — slug like `adyen` |

Do **not** call these during reframe phases. Do **not** save skim-budget drops as notes. Do **not** paste notes into `save_tailored_tex`.

1. Confirm company + role. Load `get_job_context` (JD), the tailored/master CV used for that application, and a JD-aligned `get_project_master` if stories need project depth.
